p075.lead: How one well-meant decision to take a short cut undid a planet’s plan: the default of Adam and Eve, and the declaration that there was no “fall of man.”

p075.foot.text: Presented by Solonia, the seraphic “voice in the Garden”

p075.s0.h: Introduction — A Story of Impatience, Not Malice
p075.s0.b0: Paper 75 tells the tragedy of Eden. After more than a hundred years of effort Adam could see very little progress outside the Garden, and the situation seemed so desperate as to call for some relief not embraced in the original plans. The text first makes clear that Adam and his mate were loyal. They were isolated from their kind and sorely distressed by the sorry plight of their world.
p075.s0.b1: The narrator of this paper is Solonia, the very seraphim who reproved Adam and Eve in the Garden that night. So the account reads not as a verdict pronounced from afar but as the testimony of one who stood close by. What the paper stresses again and again is not evil intent but what happens when good intentions meet wrong methods.
p075.s1.h: I. The Urantia Problem — Adam on the Hardest of Worlds
p075.s1.b0: On a normal planet the first work of Adam and Eve would be the co-ordination and blending of the races. On Urantia that project seemed just about hopeless, for the races had never been purged of their retarded and defective strains. They could not take counsel with their superiors, and the early departure of the Melchizedek receivers deepened their loneliness.

p075.s1.b2.q: Slowly their courage weakened, their spirits drooped, and sometimes their faith almost faltered.

p075.s1.b3: The narrator states plainly that they would have sometime met with success had they been more farseeing and patient. But both of them, especially Eve, were altogether too impatient and unwilling to settle down to the long endurance test. They wanted immediate results, and they got them—but those results proved most disastrous both to themselves and to their world.
p075.s2.h: II–III. Caligastia’s Plot; The Temptation of Eve
p075.s2.b0: Caligastia often visited the Garden and proposed compromises, but Adam and Eve, having seen enough of the results of rebellion, were adamant. He had no power to influence anyone against his will. So he gave up on Adam and tried a flank attack on Eve, using as his channel suitable persons from the upper strata of the Nodites, descendants of his onetime staff.
p075.s2.b1: Two things should be remembered here. Though misguided, Caligastia was still the titular Planetary Prince of Urantia, a high Son of the local universe, and was not finally deposed until the times of Christ Michael on Urantia. And from the early days of Eden the Garden dwellers had received much valuable help and co-operation from the Nodites. The danger came not from an enemy but from within a trusted partnership.
p075.s2.b2: Before leaving, the Melchizedeks had especially warned Eve never to stray from the side of her mate—to attempt no personal or secret methods of furthering their common work. Eve kept these instructions scrupulously for more than a hundred years. Yet it did not occur to her that any danger could attach to her increasingly private and confidential visits with a Nodite leader named Serapatatia.

p075.s2.b3.q: The whole affair developed so gradually and naturally that she was taken unawares.

p075.s2.b4: Serapatatia was no villain. Impressed by the righteousness of Adam’s cause, he brought his people into affiliation with the work of the Garden and became one of Adam’s ablest lieutenants. The text twice insists that he was entirely honest and sincere and never knew he was being used as a tool of Caligastia. But he too was impatient; he wanted to see results within his own lifetime.

p075.s2.b6.q: Before she quite realized what was transpiring, the fatal step had been taken.

p075.s3.h: IV. The Realization of Default — Commingling Good and Evil
p075.s3.b0: The celestial life of the planet was astir, and Adam called Eve aside and heard for the first time the whole story: a plan to speed world improvement in two directions at once, pursuing the divine plan alongside Serapatatia’s enterprise. Then “⟦Q 75:4.2⟧the voice in the Garden⟦/Q⟧”—the narrator herself—announced that they had transgressed the Garden covenant, disobeyed the Melchizedeks, and defaulted on their oaths of trust to the sovereign of the universe.

p075.s3.b2: This definition is the heart of the paper. Eve did not act from rebellious intent. Cano assured her that men and women with good motives could do no evil, but the text overturns exactly that idea. However high the motive, an attempt to reach righteous ends by the wrong way, departing from the divine plan, is evil.

p075.s3.b3.q: it constituted evil because it represented the wrong way to achieve righteous ends, because it departed from the right way, the divine plan.

p075.s3.b4: That night the narrator spoke with the two and gave them counsel; some of it they followed and some they disregarded. This conference survives in the records as the Lord God calling to Adam and Eve in the Garden, “⟦Q 75:4.8⟧Where are you?⟦/Q⟧” Later generations tended to attribute everything extraordinary to the direct intervention of the Gods.
p075.s4.h: V–VI. Repercussions of Default; Adam and Eve Leave the Garden
p075.s4.b0: Heartbroken as he was, Adam held only pity and sympathy for Eve. The next day he sought out Laotta, a Nodite woman, and committed the same folly. The text makes clear that he was not beguiled but deliberately chose to share Eve’s fate; he could not bear the thought of a lonely vigil on Urantia without her.

p075.s4.b1.q: he deliberately chose to share the fate of Eve.

p075.s4.b2: The consequences followed one upon another. The infuriated Garden dwellers destroyed the nearby Nodite settlement, and Serapatatia, overcome with remorse, drowned himself. Adam wandered alone for thirty days while Eve and the children knew nothing of his fate. Only when the Melchizedek receivers returned seventy days after the default did Adam know for certain that they had failed. A long and bitter war with the Nodites began at this time.

p075.s4.b3.q: The consequences of the follies of misguided parents are so often shared by their innocent children.

p075.s4.b4: Those thirty days, the text says, were as long years of suffering to Eve. She did not know whether her mate had destroyed himself in sorrow or been removed from the world in retribution, and no later hardship ever compared with those nights of loneliness. So when Adam returned, her joy and gratitude were never effaced through all their long partnership. Even after the misstep, love was not broken.
p075.s4.b5: As the Nodite host advanced, Adam, who had no liking for war, left the first garden unopposed with some twelve hundred loyal followers. On the third day the seraphic transports arrived, and the children of the age of choice were given the option of staying or going to Edentia. Two thirds chose Edentia, and all the younger children were taken there as well. Before finding a new home, the pair had lost more than three fourths of their children.
p075.s5.h: VII. Degradation of Adam and Eve — Default, Not Rebellion
p075.s5.b0: Gabriel appeared to pronounce judgment: the Planetary Adam and Eve were adjudged in default, having violated the covenant of their trusteeship. They were reduced to the status of mortals and must henceforth look to the future of the world races for their own future as man and woman of Urantia. Yet the judges on Salvington absolved them of all charges of “⟦Q 75:7.2⟧contempt of the universe government.⟦/Q⟧”

p075.s5.b2.q: What they had done was indeed evil, but they were never guilty of contempt for truth, neither did they knowingly enlist in rebellion against the righteous rule of the Universal Father and his Creator Son.

p075.s6.h: VIII. The So-Called Fall of Man — Perfection Is the Goal, Not the Origin
p075.s6.b0: The final section corrects an old theological notion. Adam and Eve did fall from the high estate of material sonship to the status of mortal man, but that was not the fall of man. The history of the human race is one of progressive evolution, and the Adamic bestowal left the world’s peoples biologically far better off than before. The superior stocks of Urantia now carry inheritance factors from four sources: Andonite, Sangik, Nodite, and Adamic.

p075.s6.b1.q: There has been no “fall of man.”

p075.s6.b2: Adam, the text says, should not be regarded as the cause of a curse on the human race; justice demands recognition that he faced a well-nigh hopeless task. And from this story it draws a lesson for every ascender: nothing is gained by impatiently trying to circumvent the divine plan through short cuts or personal inventions.

p075.s6.b3.q: Never, in all your ascent to Paradise, will you gain anything by impatiently attempting to circumvent the established and divine plan by short cuts, personal inventions, or other devices

p075.s6.b4.q: Perfection is our eternal goal, not our origin.

p075.s6.b5: The narrator even rejoices that mistakes and disagreements are possible, because they show that this universe is dominated not by mechanism but by personality. Because the universe is personal and progressive, failure can happen—and for the same reason we can be confident of growth, experience, and adventure.
p075.s7.b0: Paper 75 is a record of failure, but not of condemnation. In isolation, loneliness, and discouragement, good people took a short cut for good ends, and the result wounded everyone. Yet the text says that humanity was not fallen but uplifted, and that ours is a personal universe able to hold even mistakes. The paper warns us against impatience while teaching us to look on those who fail with compassion.

p075.s7.b2: Paper 76 tells of the second garden that Adam and Eve founded in the Euphrates valley after leaving Eden, and of the rest of their lives as mortals. Reading of the service they continued after their failure shows how the tragedy of this paper leads on into a story of recovery.
p076.lead: The second garden raised between the Tigris and Euphrates: the tragedy of Cain and Abel, the life of the violet race, and Adam and Eve, who died as mortals and rose as ascenders.

p076.foot.text: Presented by Solonia, the seraphic “voice in the Garden”

p076.s0.b0: Paper 76 is the last chapter in the story of Adam and Eve. Where the previous paper dealt with the moment of default, this one deals with the life that followed. Having left the first garden to the Nodites, Adam’s company could not go west for lack of boats, nor north because the Nodites were on the march, nor south because of hostile tribes. Only the east lay open, and they journeyed toward the pleasant lands between the Tigris and Euphrates.
p076.s0.b1: Cain and Sansa were born before the caravan reached its destination. Laotta, Sansa’s mother, died in childbirth; Eve suffered much but survived, and she took Sansa to her bosom and reared her along with Cain. Sansa grew into a woman of great ability and became the wife of Sargan, chief of the northern blue races. The mood of the paper begins here, with Eve embracing even the child born of her mate’s misstep.
p076.s1.h: I. The Edenites Enter Mesopotamia — By the Sweat of Their Faces
p076.s1.b0: The caravan took almost a full year to reach the Euphrates, and finding it in flood they camped nearly six weeks before crossing. Hearing that the king and high priest of Eden was coming, the inhabitants fled to the eastern mountains, and Adam found the land vacated. The site had been one of the three original choices of Van and Amadon’s committee, and to the north, where the two rivers came close together, a defense wall of fifty-six miles could be built.

p076.s1.b1.q: They found the first garden partially prepared for them, but the second had to be created by the labor of their own hands and in the “sweat of their faces.”

p076.s2.h: II. Cain and Abel — Environment and Repentance
p076.s2.b0: Abel was the first child of Adam and Eve born in the second garden. At twelve he chose to be a herder, while Cain had chosen agriculture, and each brought offerings to the priests. Abel noticed that his animal sacrifices were preferred and taunted his brother. Cain’s appeal to the first Eden’s preference for the fruits of the field had a justifiable precedent, for Adam had in fact sought to discourage animal sacrifice.
p076.s2.b1: There was a reason it turned out this way. Burdened with building, defense, and agriculture, and much depressed spiritually, Adam had entrusted worship and education to men of Nodite extraction, who soon reverted to pre-Adamic standards. Abel, moreover, never failed to remind Cain that Adam was not his father. When Cain was twenty and Abel eighteen, Abel’s taunts so infuriated Cain that he turned on him and slew him.

p076.s2.b2.q: Good social environment and proper education are indispensable soil and atmosphere for getting the most out of a good inheritance.

p076.s2.b3: Through Abel the text speaks of the weight of environment and education. Abel had an ideal inheritance, but the unfavorable surroundings of his youth virtually neutralized it; had he lived to twenty-five or thirty, he would have become an entirely different person. The observation that a bad environment can effectively spoil an excellent inheritance, at least in the younger years, speaks directly to parents and teachers today.
p076.s2.b4: Cain’s story leads to repentance. As a living symbol of the default he felt the unspoken resentment of those around him, and out of fear and some remorse he went to his mother Eve for spiritual help. When he honestly sought divine assistance, an Adjuster—never before present—came to indwell him. Cain went east to the land of Nod, became a great leader among one group of his father’s people, and throughout his life promoted peace between the Nodites and the Adamites.

p076.s2.b5.q: But he now went to Eve, his mother, and asked for spiritual help and guidance, and when he honestly sought divine assistance, an Adjuster indwelt him.

p076.s3.h: III. Life in Mesopotamia — Raising the Next Generation
p076.s3.b0: Adam and Eve greatly missed their former home and the children taken to Edentia, yet they bore their diminished estate with grace and fortitude. Adam spent most of his time training his children and associates in civil administration, educational methods, and religious devotion, and thanks to that foresight his death made little difference to the conduct of his people’s affairs.

p076.s3.b1.q: Had it not been for this foresight, pandemonium would have broken loose upon his death.

p076.s3.b3: The Sethite priesthood was a threefold undertaking of religion, health, and education: its priests officiated at ceremonies, served as physicians and sanitary inspectors, and taught in the schools. The text asks us not to confuse them with the debased and commercial priesthoods of later times. The Adamites produced the third alphabet, maintained writing, metalworking, pottery, and weaving, and left an architecture not excelled for thousands of years.

p076.s3.b4.q: Their religious concepts of Deity and the universe were advanced and more or less accurate, their health provisions were, for their time, excellent, and their methods of education have never since been surpassed.

p076.s4.h: IV. The Violet Race — Traits and Legacy of the Ninth Race
p076.s4.b0: Adam and Eve were the founders of the violet race, the ninth human race to appear on Urantia. The text records its physical traits and abilities, noting that they came from Adam’s life plasm and diminished with each succeeding generation. These traits may be summarized as follows.

p076.s4.b2: The text traces the persistence of fear and the struggle with so many diseases in present-day races to the fact that, owing to the early miscarriage of the uplift plans, our ancestors received so little of Adam’s life plasm. Adam tried to make up a little of this. A commission of twelve headed by Eve selected 1,682 women from the surrounding tribes, and 1,570 of their children grew to maturity. Reared among their mothers’ tribes, they formed the early beginnings of the Andite race.
p076.s4.b3: There is a note on diet as well. Adam and Eve and their first generation of children ate no meat, living on “⟦Q 76:4.4⟧the fruits of the trees⟦/Q⟧”; later descendants took dairy products, but many kept to a nonflesh diet, and most of these vegetarian tribes later moved east and mingled with the peoples of India. Eve, the text adds, did not suffer pain in childbirth; the severe pangs belonged only to the mixed races.
p076.s5.h: V. Death of Adam and Eve — Repentance, the Adjuster, and Michael’s Promise
p076.s5.b0: Not long after the second Eden was founded, Adam and Eve were told that their repentance was acceptable and that they would be eligible to join the sleeping survivors. Their transgression had been an error of judgment, not the sin of deliberate rebellion. They had had no Adjusters as citizens of Jerusem or in the first garden, but soon after their reduction to mortal status they became conscious of a new presence within them.

p076.s5.b1.q: they knew that they had failed as Material Sons of Satania, but they also knew that the Paradise career was still open to them as ascending sons of the universe.

p076.s5.b2: A comfort and also a mystery to them was the one personal message they ever received from Michael: a promise to call them from mortal slumber when he came to Urantia. They could not fully grasp its meaning, but they proclaimed that a Son of God would someday come, and Adam cherished the hope that strife-torn Urantia might yet become the envied planet of all Nebadon. Adam lived 530 years and died of old age; Eve had died nineteen years earlier of a weakened heart.
p076.s5.b3: They were buried in the center of the temple built to their plans soon after the colony’s wall was finished. The text says this was the origin of the practice of burying noted and pious men and women beneath the floors of places of worship.
p076.s5.b4: With Adam’s default ended a regime of physical representatives of the universe government that had lasted more than four hundred and fifty thousand years. No comprehensive plan for world welfare was proclaimed until Machiventa Melchizedek came in the times of Abraham. Yet the text says misfortune was not Urantia’s only lot, for that very background of darkness drew Michael to choose this world as the arena for revealing the Father’s love.

p076.s5.b5.q: it is rather that the evil and sin on Urantia afforded the Creator Son a more striking background against which to reveal the matchless love, mercy, and patience of the Paradise Father.

p076.s6.h: VI. Survival of Adam and Eve — Leaving as Sons of God, Returning as Sons of Man
p076.s6.b0: Adam and Eve did not sleep long. On the third day after Adam’s death a special roll call was ordered by Lanaforge, and the pair were repersonalized in the resurrection halls of the mansion worlds of Satania together with 1,316 of their associates from the first garden. They passed quickly through the worlds of ascension to citizenship on Jerusem, and they now belong to the four and twenty counselors, the advisory-control body of Urantia.

p076.s6.b1.q: They left Jerusem as permanent citizens—Sons of God; they returned as ascendant citizens—sons of man.

p076.s6.b3.q: It is the people who make a civilization; civilization does not make the people.

p076.s7.b0: The narrator sums up the story of Adam and Eve as one of trial, tragedy, and triumph. They failed as Material Sons, but they repented, received Adjusters, entered the path of ascending sons, and at last returned to help the very world on which they had failed. Failure is not the end; it can be the starting point of another road to the same destination. That is the conclusion of the four-paper story of Eden.

p076.s7.b3: Paper 77 turns to beings who have worked beside these stories all along: the midway creatures. It is good to read it remembering the part they played, from the days of Van and Amadon through the preparation of the Garden and the crisis of Adam.
p077.lead: Permanent citizens of the planet, born between mortals and angels: the origin and rebellion of the primary and secondary midwayers, and their united service today.

p077.foot.text: Presented by an Archangel of Nebadon

p077.s0.b0: In Paper 77 an Archangel of Nebadon introduces the midway creatures of Urantia. They are a unique group existing on a life-functioning level about midway between mortals and the angelic orders. They may seem an accident of time, yet they are accepted as one of the essential orders of planetary ministry. On Urantia there are two orders: the primary midwayers, who appeared in the days of Dalamatia, and the secondary midwayers, whose origin dates from the times of Adam.

p077.s0.b1.q: existing on a life-functioning level about midway between those of the mortals of the realms and of the angelic orders; hence are they called midway creatures.

p077.s0.b2: The paper follows two lines of descent. After telling of the birth of the primary midwayers, it turns back to the Nodites and the tower of Babel, who supplied half the ancestry of the secondary midwayers, and then to Adamson and Ratta, who supplied the other half. It then treats in turn the rebellion, the union of the two orders, and their mission as permanent citizens.
p077.s1.h: I. The Primary Midwayers — An Origin Hard to Explain
p077.s1.b0: The one hundred corporeal members of Prince Caligastia’s staff were, as morontia citizens of Jerusem, supermaterial beings without reproductive prerogatives, yet as ministers on Urantia they were material sex creatures. The narrator frankly admits being unable to explain satisfactorily how they could function as parents on a supermaterial level. But that is exactly what happened.

p077.s1.b1.q: A supermaterial (nonsexual) liaison of a male and a female member of the corporeal staff resulted in the appearance of the first-born of the primary midwayers.

p077.s1.b2: Once the usefulness of the first fifty was established, the Prince, after a year of observation, authorized reproduction without restriction. Each couple produced one every half year until a thousand had been born to it, and then the power was exhausted; thus came the original corps of 50,000. They served as the intelligence corps of the Prince’s administration, ranging far and wide to study the races. The rebellion ensnared a little over four fifths of them, and the loyal corps served the Melchizedek receivers under the leadership of Van.
p077.s2.h: II. The Nodite Race — An Eighth Race from Modified Germ Plasm
p077.s2.b0: Because the staff carried germ plasm of the Andonic strains, their offspring were expected to resemble other Andonite children. But when the sixty rebels who followed Nod had children, an unexpected difference appeared. The text traces it to the life circuits of the Satania system acting in the bodies of the staff and altering the germ plasm, likening the process to the way scientists modify germ plasm with X rays.

p077.s2.b1.q: This unexpected excellence characterized not only physical and intellectual qualities but also spiritual capacities.

p077.s2.b2: The sixty rebel staff members and the forty-four modified Andonites who joined the rebellion—104 in all—became the ancestors of the Nodites, the eighth race of Urantia. They gradually mingled with the evolutionary peoples, and ten thousand years after the rebellion their life span was little more than that of the other races. The text explains the long reigns of the Sumerian king lists and the record of a man who lived over nine hundred “years” as traditions arising from the long lives of early rulers and from confusing the twenty-eight-day month with the year.
p077.s2.b3: The ancient tale of “⟦Q 77:2.3⟧sons of the gods⟦/Q⟧” taking the daughters of men also begins here. Evolutionary mortals regarded the staff and their descendants in that way, and tradition even magnified their stature. It is an interpretation that finds traces of real history at the bottom of myth.
p077.s3.h: III. The Tower of Babel — A Community Divided over Purpose
p077.s3.b0: After Dalamatia sank, the Nodites founded Dilmun. About fifty thousand years after Nod’s death, as their numbers grew and intermarriage with neighboring tribes spread, the leaders adopted the plan of Bablot and began a temple with a great tower. But after four and one-half years a bitter dispute arose over the purpose of the tower, and all work stopped.

p077.s3.b3: The majority resented the teaching that their ancestors had rebelled as a racial stigma. About twelve thousand years ago the Andites tried to raise a new temple on the ruins, but it too failed. The lesson of this section is that a plan to glorify ourselves scattered the community.
p077.s4.b0: The internal war over the tower dispersed the Nodites, and their culture declined for over one hundred and twenty thousand years until the Adamic infusion. Even so, in the times of Adam they were still an able people, and members of this line were among the Garden builders and on Adam’s staff.

The northern Vanites taught that their seven commandments had been given to Van on Mount Ararat, and these regional traditions were later woven into the story of Noah’s flood.
p077.s5.h: V–VI. Adamson and Ratta; The Secondary Midwayers
p077.s5.b0: The other half of the secondary midwayers’ ancestry comes from Adam’s eldest son, Adamson. He set out with twenty-seven companions in search of the northern highland people he had heard of from Van and Amadon, and after a little over three years he found and married Ratta, who claimed to be the last pure-line descendant of the Prince’s staff. His departure was pleasant, yet Adam and Eve grieved deeply at losing their eldest son.
p077.s5.b1: The couple had sixty-seven children, and every fourth child was of a unique order, often invisible. Ratta was greatly perturbed, but Adamson, knowing of the primary midwayers, concluded that something similar was happening, and he mated these children.

p077.s5.b2.q: this is the origin of the secondary order of midwayers.

p077.s5.b3: Sixteen of these unique children formed eight couples, each able by a combined sex and nonsex liaison to produce a secondary midwayer every seventy days; each couple produced 248, for a total of 1,984. The sixteen parents lived and died as mortals, but their offspring live on, free of the limitations of the flesh. With these helpers the Adamsonites maintained a high culture for almost seven thousand years.

p077.s5.b4.q: And such a phenomenon was never possible on earth before that time, nor has it ever occurred since.

p077.s8.b0: The seraphim come and go, but the midwayers remain. As natives and ministers of the planet they provide the one continuing regime that links the changing seraphic administrations. Any of them could leave the planet, but they have pledged not to until released, and the only loyal midwayer ever to depart Urantia is 1-2-3 the first, now one of the twenty-four counselors on Jerusem.

p077.s8.b1.q: Their determination is suggested by the motto of their order: “What the United Midwayers undertake, the United Midwayers do.”

p077.s8.b2: Midwayers are brought into being fully developed, yet they never cease to grow in wisdom and experience. p078.s0.h: Introduction — The History of a Vanished Cradle
p078.s0.b0: Paper 78 covers the span from about 35,000 B.C., soon after Adam’s default, to about 2000 B.C., when the violet race finally disappeared from its Mesopotamian homelands. It is presented by an Archangel of Nebadon. Its central stage is the second garden between the Tigris and Euphrates, and its protagonists are the Adamites and the Andites they became as they blended with other peoples.

p078.s0.b1.q: The second Eden was the cradle of civilization for almost thirty thousand years.

p078.s1.b0: When Adam arrived, the physical evolution of the races had gone on unaffected by the rebellion, but minds and morals were at a low level. Though partially a failure, Adam’s contribution greatly upstepped the peoples. Still, thirty-five thousand years ago most of the world had little culture, with centers of civilization scattered here and there.

p078.s1.b3: Having drawn this map, the text calls it the world just before the great expansions of the violet race some twenty-five thousand years ago. The hope of future civilization lay in the second garden between the rivers, where the ideas and ideals salvaged from Dalamatia and Eden had the potential to spread to all the world. The progeny Adam and Eve left behind was limited in number, but potent.
p078.s2.h: II. The Adamites in the Second Garden — The Fate of a Borrowed Civilization
p078.s2.b0: For thousands of years Adam’s descendants worked on irrigation and flood control to the south and on defenses to the north, striving to preserve the traditions of the first Eden. Never losing sight of the purpose of their mission, they sent their choicest sons and daughters as emissaries to the other races. At times this depleted their home culture, but always they recovered.

p078.s2.b1.q: But the civilization of the second Eden was an artificial structure—it had not been evolved—and was therefore doomed to deteriorate until it reached a natural evolutionary level.

p078.s2.b2: Adam left a great intellectual and spiritual culture but no advanced mechanical appliances. Every civilization, the text explains, is limited by natural resources, inherent genius, and leisure for invention. A culture resting on Adam’s presence and the traditions of Eden settled, as those traditions faded, to a level in balance with its surroundings. It invites us to consider that what is given from above lasts longest when a foundation grown from within supports it.
p078.s2.b3: This does not mean the second garden was small or weak. Around 19,000 B.C. the Adamites were a real nation of four and a half million, and they had already poured millions of descendants into the surrounding peoples. The decline was not a sudden collapse but a gentle descent over thousands of years.
p078.s3.h: III. Early Expansions of the Adamites — Sending Teachers Instead of Conquering
p078.s3.b0: The violet race long kept the peaceful traditions of Eden, so even as their population grew they did not make war for land. The cultural effect of these early migrations did not last, but those who went out as teachers, traders, and explorers brought biologic vigor to the peoples around them.

p078.s3.b1.q: instead of making war to secure more territory, they sent forth their excess inhabitants as teachers to the other races.

p078.s3.b2: The main current of migration went north, circled the Caspian, and turned west into Europe. But the farther they went, the more the Adamic traits thinned, and their culture was largely lost in transit. Only the later Andites moved fast enough to carry the culture of Eden far from Mesopotamia.

p078.s4.h: IV. The Andites — A Versatile People Born of Blending
p078.s4.b0: The Andites were the primary blends of the violet race and the Nodites plus the evolutionary peoples; the term generally designates peoples whose inheritance was from one-eighth to one-sixth violet. They arose on the outer edge of the concentric circles surrounding the second garden and spread northward as they blended with the inhabitants of Turkestan.

p078.s4.b1.q: These early Andites were not Aryan; they were pre-Aryan.

p078.s4.b2: The text adds that they were not white, and neither Occidental nor Oriental. We may read this as a warning not to project today’s racial categories onto the past. It also records that as the peaceful violet tradition joined with the belligerent Nodite stock, their movements became increasingly military. The character of a culture is not fixed; it changes with blending and with choices.
p078.s4.b3: The Andites were adventurous and had roving dispositions. Mixture with other stocks steadied them somewhat, yet their descendants never stopped until they had circumnavigated the globe and found the last remote continent. That persistent movement toward new places laid out the paths along which civilization later spread.
p078.s5.h: V–VI. The Andite Migrations; The Last Andite Dispersions
p078.s5.b0: Around 15,000 B.C. the revival of the Sethite priesthood made the Garden shine again, and great waves of civilization spread over Eurasia and North Africa. In the highlands of Turkestan languages blended to form the so-called Aryan mother tongue. One hundred and thirty-two Andites sailed from Japan in small boats, crossed the Pacific, and reached South America, and Easter Island was long a center of one of these lost groups.

p078.s5.b1.q: And to every nation to which they journeyed, they contributed humor, art, adventure, music, and manufacture.

p078.s5.b2: By 12,000 B.C. three quarters of the world’s Andites lived in northern and eastern Europe. They went also to northern China and India, and as missionaries, teachers, and traders to the ends of the earth. The text identifies them as the so-called Dravidian and later Aryan conquerors of India, and records that some went to China by way of Sinkiang and Tibet.
p078.s5.b3: Between 8000 and 6000 B.C., pressed by the hill tribes to the east and the plainsmen to the west, the last three waves left Mesopotamia. They divided as follows.

p078.s5.b5: These migrations drained the biologic reserves of the homeland while greatly strengthening the surrounding peoples. The cultural age of the second garden came to an end, and civilization moved west to the Nile and the Mediterranean islands.
p078.s6.h: VII. The Floods in Mesopotamia — The Real Story of Noah
p078.s6.b0: From about 5000 B.C. the northern highlands rose rapidly and snowfall increased, bringing unprecedented floods to the Euphrates valley every spring. For almost a thousand years scores of cities were deserted, and these floods completed the disruption of Andite civilization.

p078.s6.b1.q: There has never been a universal flood since life was established on Urantia.

p078.s6.b2: The text explains that the story of a world-wide flood was devised by Hebrew priests in the Babylonian captivity to connect their genealogies. Yet it affirms that Noah himself was real. He was a wine maker of Aram near Erech who kept a yearly record of the river’s rise and was ridiculed for urging that houses be built like boats. When one year unusually heavy rains swept away the village, only his family survived in their houseboat.
p078.s7.h: VIII. The Sumerians—Last of the Andites
p078.s7.b0: The small minority who remained at the river mouths were the Sumerians. Even when horse-riding invaders from the northeast overran the whole valley, they kept their integrity for a long time thanks to superior intelligence, better weapons, their system of military canals, and a uniform group religion. The invaders soon came to trust these peaceful people as teachers and administrators.

p078.s7.b1.q: Each city believed its municipal god to be superior to all other gods, and therefore they refused to subordinate themselves to a common leader.

p078.s7.b2: After their confederation broke up, the city-states were ruled by apostate descendants of the Sethite priests and, jealous over their city gods, could not unite. Sargon of Kish ended that era, but struggles for supremacy went on, and about 2500 B.C. Lagash fell. By the time of Hammurabi the Sumerians had been absorbed by the northern Semites. The contrast is striking: a people once protected by a united faith lost its strength along with that unity.
p078.s7.b3: The northern tribes who took the valley willingly absorbed what remained of Mesopotamian civilization, adopting Sumerian culture and the arts of the valley. They even tried to build a third tower of Babel and took its name for their nation. What the barbarians failed to do to ruin Mesopotamia, the text adds, later climatic changes accomplished.
p078.s8.b0: The homeland of the violet race vanished amid emigration, immigration, flood, and invasion. Yet the text does not end on mere decline. Long before the horsemen conquered the valley, the culture of the Garden had already spread across three continents, becoming the leaven that shaped today’s civilization.

p079.lead: From Turkestan to India and China: the eastward expansion of the Andites and the different roads taken by the civilizations of those lands.

p079.foot.text: Presented by an Archangel of Nebadon

p079.s0.h: Introduction — Asia, the Homeland of Humankind
p079.s0.b0: Paper 79 carries the Andite story of Paper 78 eastward. It is presented by an Archangel of Nebadon. Asia was where Andon and Fonta were born, where the Sangik peoples branched off, and where the civilizations from Dalamatia to the Andites arose. This paper compares the roads taken by three parts of that continent: central Asia, India, and China.

p079.s0.b1.q: Asia is the homeland of the human race.

p079.s0.b2: This paper often assesses racial mixture and relative superiority. The commentary presents those statements only within the text’s own scope and does not use them as grounds for judging any people today. Indeed, the conclusion the paper keeps returning to is that the higher power deciding a civilization’s destiny is true religion and the pursuit of truth.
p079.s1.h: I. The Andites of Turkestan — The Rise of Traders and Cities
p079.s1.b0: For over twenty-five thousand years the heart of Eurasia was predominantly Andite. From the lowlands of Turkestan they turned west into Europe; from the highlands they moved through Sinkiang and Tibet into China, and through the Punjab and Baluchistan into India. These early movements were no conquests but a steady drifting. For almost fifteen thousand years the Tarim basin was the easternmost outpost of Andite culture, rivaling Mesopotamia itself, until the rain winds shifted and it perished.
p079.s1.b1: As central Asia dried out around 8000 B.C., the Andites were driven to the valleys of the Nile, Euphrates, Indus, and Yellow rivers. Instead of turning to herding like the older races, they built cities devoted to manufacture and trade, and Adonia, near present-day Ashkhabad, became the commercial metropolis of central Asia. Environmental pressure produced not regression but a new way of life.

p079.s1.b2.q: A new class of men, the traders, began to appear in large numbers.

p079.s1.b3: Drought and the southward push of the Andonites diluted the Andites of central Asia nearly to the vanishing point, yet their traces endured. The text sees the Mongols under Genghis Khan in A.D. 1200 as the last manifestation of their military genius, adding that the early breakup of that empire delayed contact between East and West and hindered the growth of monotheism in Asia.

p079.s1.b4.q: these warriors proclaimed the existence of “one God in heaven.”

p079.s2.h: II–III. The Andite Conquest of India; Dravidian India
p079.s2.b0: India is the only place where all the Urantia races were blended. From about 15,000 B.C., for more than fifteen centuries, Andites poured in through Baluchistan and spread over the Indus and Ganges valleys. The text finds the main reason India did not lead Eurasia in its topography: people were crowded south into the Deccan, surrounded by sea. Despite the conquerors’ restrictions on intermarriage, the Andites were largely absorbed by 10,000 B.C.
p079.s2.b1: This section includes the narrator’s assessment of the gains and losses of racial mixture. The text holds that mixture is advantageous because it favors versatility of culture, but that its achievements need certain conditions to endure. This is offered as a diagnosis explaining India’s history in that age, and the commentary adds no further generalization.
p079.s2.b2: The blending of the Andites with the native stock produced the Dravidians, who soon built the most versatile civilization then on earth. They were among the earliest city builders; by 7000 B.C. their camel trains and ships reached Mesopotamia and the East Indies, and they brought an alphabet and the art of writing from Sumeria. Their civilization survives in the Deccan to this day.
p079.s2.b3: In religious history, too, India had a special beginning. The thread of monotheism in Indian religion stems from the teachings of the second garden, and as early as 16,000 B.C. one hundred Sethite priests entered India and very nearly won the western half of it. But their teaching did not last.

p079.s2.b4.q: Within five thousand years their doctrines of the Paradise Trinity had degenerated into the triune symbol of the fire god.

p079.s3.h: IV. The Aryan Invasion of India — What Caste Could Not Preserve
p079.s3.b0: In the middle of the third millennium before Christ, the Aryan invasion—the last great migration out of Turkestan—went on for nearly five hundred years. Too few to complete the conquest, the Aryans were absorbed by the Dravidians of the south, and except in the north their influence was chiefly cultural and religious. On the Gangetic plain the two streams mingled to produce a high culture.

The Aryans brought concepts of Deity preserved from the religion of the second garden, but the Brahman priests could not withstand the pagan momentum of sudden contact with the religions of the Deccan. This, the text says, is why India failed to produce the high civilization once foreshadowed.

p079.s3.b3.q: for religion, true religion, is the indispensable source of that higher energy which drives men to establish a superior civilization based on human brotherhood.

p079.s3.b4: What institutional walls sought to protect was not protected; the power that lifts a civilization comes in the end from true religion. That is the conclusion of this section. And the text leaves a hope.

p079.s4.h: V. Red Man and Yellow Man — The Long Struggle for Asia
p079.s4.b0: The story of eastern Asia belongs to the primary Sangiks, the red and yellow races. The red man was first to form tribal organization and reigned in eastern Asia for almost a hundred thousand years before the yellow tribes arrived. The yellow race, entering China along the coast more than three hundred thousand years ago, pushed northward, and the two races fought for more than two hundred thousand years. At first the red men generally prevailed, but the yellow man learned the art of war and showed a marked ability to live peaceably with his own people.

p079.s4.b1.q: the Chinese were the first to learn that in union there is strength.

p079.s4.b2: The red tribes, torn by internal conflict, left Asia when the Bering isthmus opened, and the last pure red men departed eighty-five thousand years ago. The red and yellow races are the only stocks that achieved a high civilization apart from Andite influence, and the peoples of the Western Hemisphere remained nearly isolated from the rest of the world until the end of the first millennium after Christ. From the same starting point, the results diverged between those who co-operated and those who divided.
p079.s4.b3: The civilizations of the Americas were evolutionary products of the Sangiks. The oldest Amerindian culture was the Onamonalonton center in California, and more enduring civilizations later arose in Mexico, Central America, and the mountains of South America. The text reveals that the original Melchizedek plan stipulated that one million pure-line descendants of Adam should go to upstep the red men of the Americas—a glimpse of the distance between the original plan and the history that actually unfolded.
p079.s5.h: VI–VII. Dawn of Chinese Civilization; The Andites Enter China
p079.s5.b0: After driving out the red man, the Chinese had by twenty thousand years ago built a dozen centers of culture along the Yellow River and the Yangtze. The text sums up the reasons the ancient yellow race moved ahead under four factors.

p079.s5.b2.q: The stimulus of a progressive and advanced religion is often a decisive factor in cultural development

p079.s5.b3: In 15,000 B.C. the Chinese numbered fewer than twelve million, yet as a compact body speaking a common language they formed a nation more united than any of their political unions in historic times. From 25,000 to 5000 B.C. the highest mass civilization on Urantia was in central and northern China. But for the mountain barriers and a later decline in spiritual culture, the text adds, the yellow race would quickly have dominated world civilization.
p079.s5.b4: About fifteen thousand years ago Andites crossed the pass of Ti Tao into the upper Yellow River valley. Though few, their mixture produced a more versatile stock, and the Yellow River settlements forged ahead of the Yangtze villages. The text judges that this limited infusion did not disturb the stability of the Sangik type. Cities and manufacture began after 10,000 B.C., and Chinese merchants traveled to Mesopotamia even in Sumerian days, to the benefit of both.
p079.s6.h: VIII. Later Chinese Civilization — The Light and Shadow of Ancestor Veneration
p079.s6.b0: With external threats gone, the old military state dissolved and a peaceful society of agriculture and family took its place. Pride in past achievements, the conservatism of a farming people, and a well-developed family life gave birth to ancestor veneration. Then the search for new truth became overshadowed by a tendency to venerate what was already established.

p079.s6.b1.q: Slowly the genius of the yellow race became diverted from the pursuit of the unknown to the preservation of the known.

p079.s6.b4: Truth, the text says, is relative and expanding and lives always in the present. At the same time it praises the amazing stability of Chinese culture as the fruit of the paramount place given the family. Vestiges of a real concept of God survived in the imperial worship of Shang-ti, and in family loyalty, group ethics, and personal morality no civilization has excelled the Chinese.
p079.s7.b0: Paper 79 sets three regions side by side and shows that civilization is not decided by bloodline or terrain alone. p080.lead: To the Mediterranean and Europe, the Nile and the Aegean: the civilizations and declines the Andites left as they spread westward, and the origin of the blended white peoples.

p080.foot.text: Presented by an Archangel of Nebadon

p080.s0.h: Introduction — The Waves That Flowed West
p080.s0.b0: Paper 80 is the companion of Paper 79, tracing how the Andites spread to the west. It is presented by an Archangel of Nebadon. The text sums up that the European blue man did not of himself achieve a great civilization, yet when blended with Adamite and Andite strains he became the basis of one of the most potent stocks for aggressive civilization. The modern white peoples carry Adamic strains together with several Sangik strains, as well as Andonite and Nodite blood.
p080.s0.b1: This paper records harsh events such as conquest and extermination more than once. The commentary presents them calmly as historical facts reported by the text and in no way treats any group’s deeds as an example to follow. It is also worth keeping in mind that at the end of the paper the text itself declares it a fallacy to divide the white peoples into a few types.
p080.s1.b0: Even before the last Andites left the Euphrates valley, many of their kin had entered Europe as adventurers, teachers, traders, and warriors. The Mediterranean was then an inland trough closed by the Gibraltar isthmus and the Sicilian land bridge, and there blue men, Saharans, Nodites, and Adamites met and began early maritime commerce. Egypt received Mesopotamians for more than thirty thousand years, but a great influx of Saharans brought it to its lowest cultural level some fifteen thousand years ago.
p080.s1.b1: The text gives several reasons the Adamites turned toward Europe. The red and yellow races were too far away; the blue men of Europe had no religious practices the Adamites found repulsive; and there was strong attraction between the two peoples. Above all, the paths of migration were favorable. As a result, the early waves of Mesopotamian culture flowed almost entirely into Europe.

p080.s1.b2.q: And it was these circumstances that determined the antecedents of modern European civilization.

p080.s2.h: II. Climatic and Geologic Changes — Roads Closed and Roads Opened
p080.s2.b0: As the northern ice fields retreated, the rain-bearing west winds shifted north, and the open pastures of the Sahara turned to desert. The dwellers of the Sahara plateau dispersed, and their traces remain in a certain kinship among peoples from the Deccan to both shores of the Mediterranean.

p080.s2.b2: About the same time England separated from the continent and Denmark rose from the sea. An earthquake broke the Gibraltar isthmus, quickly raising the inland lake to the level of the Atlantic, and the Sicilian land bridge also sank, making the Mediterranean one sea.

p080.s2.b3.q: This cataclysm of nature flooded scores of human settlements and occasioned the greatest loss of life by flood in all the world’s history.

p080.s2.b4: With the western route closed, the Adamites pushed north and east and entered Europe from the east by way of Turkestan. The culture of the blue man they found there lagged thousands of years behind Asia’s, having been almost entirely cut off from Mesopotamia. Terrain and climate set the pace at which civilization spread.
p080.s3.h: III. The Cro-Magnoid Blue Man — Honest and Courageous Artists
p080.s3.b0: The blue men lived along the rivers of Europe and were already a highly blended people thirty-five thousand years ago. The early post-Adamic civilization of Europe was a blend of the vigor and art of the blue men with the creative imagination of the Adamites. The text records both the light and the shadow of this meeting.

p080.s3.b2.q: The blue men were perfectly honest in all their dealings and were wholly free from the sexual vices of the mixed Adamites.

p080.s3.b3: About fifteen thousand years ago, as the rain winds moved north, the grasslands of Europe became forests, and hunters turned into herders, fishers, and farmers. The text says this change brought cultural advance along with biologic retrogression, because settled life led them to keep captives as slaves. The retrogression lasted until a fresh impetus came from the east.
p080.s4.h: IV–V. The Andite Invasions of Europe; The Andite Conquest of Northern Europe
p080.s4.b0: The Andites entered Europe in seven major invasions, the last arriving on horseback in three great waves. The early expansions of the violet race had been peaceful, but the union of the peaceful Adamites with the belligerent Nodites, later mingled with Sangik strains, produced Andites who carried out actual military conquests.

p080.s4.b1.q: But the horse was the evolutionary factor which determined the dominance of the Andites in the Occident.

p080.s4.b2: The slower waves broke up the farther they traveled, but the mounted waves reached Europe as coherent groups still carrying their culture. Crossing the Russian plains they blended into one people, the ancestors of the so-called Nordic races. For three thousand years the military headquarters of the northern Andites was in Denmark.
p080.s4.b3: The text does not hide how harsh this conquest was. The Cro-Magnons held the Somme valley for over five hundred years before they fell, and Thor, the victor of the final battle, was later revered as a god by some groups. Those not absorbed, it records, were done away with under the form of ritual. This passage shows plainly the dark reality of the history of conquest.

p080.s4.b4.q: The blue strain contributed many sturdy traits and much physical vigor to the white races of Europe, but the humor and imagination of the blended European peoples were derived from the Andites.

p080.s4.b5: By 5000 B.C. the evolving white races were dominant throughout northern Europe, including northern Germany, northern France, and the British Isles, while central Europe was for a time held by the blue man and the round-headed Andonites of the Danube valley. The text concludes that the Andite-blue union caused a temporary lapse of civilization, but that its latent potential finally bore fruit in present-day European civilization.
p080.s5.h: VI. The Andites along the Nile — Egypt Succeeds Mesopotamia
p080.s5.b0: As the culture of the Euphrates declined, the center of civilization moved to the Nile. Around 5000 B.C. there were seven distinct groups in Egypt, all but one from Mesopotamia. In the last great exodus, skilled Andite artisans arrived and greatly advanced Egyptian metalworking.

p080.s5.b1.q: Egypt became the successor of Mesopotamia as the headquarters of the most advanced group on earth.

p080.s5.b2: The Egyptians gathered their city deities into a national system of gods and maintained a vast priesthood. Attempts to revive the Sethite teachings were short-lived. While Imhotep, an Andite architectural genius, served as prime minister, the first stone pyramid in Egypt was raised, but internal war and the influx of outside tribes set social progress back for more than five hundred years.
p080.s6.h: VII. Andites of the Mediterranean Isles — Crete and Greece
p080.s6.b0: About 12,000 B.C. a smaller-statured tribe of Andites crossed to Crete and founded a civilization skilled in textiles, metals, pottery, plumbing, and stone building. Almost two thousand years later Sato, a direct descendant of Adamson and Ratta, led a company of Adamsonites to Greece, and those who finally settled there were three hundred and seventy-five chosen people. The text explains that this lineage is why the Greeks had traditions of descent from gods.

p080.s6.b1.q: The Aegean region passed through five distinct cultural stages, each less spiritual than the preceding

p080.s6.b2: In Crete the “great mother” cult glorifying Eve spread widely, and it later entered early Christianity under the guise of the veneration of Mary. By about 6500 B.C. the spiritual heritage of the Andites had greatly declined. By 5000 B.C. the three purest strains of Adam’s descendants were in Sumeria, northern Europe, and Greece.

p080.s6.b3.q: And this decadence of Andite civilization, together with the disappearance of their religious standards, left the spiritually impoverished races of the world in a deplorable condition.

p080.s6.b4: Even amid decline the migrations did not stop. About 5000 B.C. progressive Mesopotamians settled Cyprus, only to be wiped out some two thousand years later by northern hordes, and another great colony arose near the later site of Carthage. As Egypt declined, able families moved to Crete and then on to Greece. The Greeks were not only great teachers and artists but the world’s greatest traders and colonizers, planting many outposts of culture to the west.
p080.s7.b0: Between the two branches of the white race that spread north and west lay the broad-headed descendants of the Andonites in the central mountain regions; the ancient Hittites came from this stock. The Danubians, who moved north through the Balkans along the Danube, were farmers and herders who made pottery, and they deteriorated rapidly as they moved away from the source of their culture. Through missionaries from Crete they became mother worshipers, and they practiced cremation of the dead.
p080.s8.h: IX. The Three White Races — and the Limits of Classification
p080.s8.b0: Toward the close of the Andite migrations the blends in Europe became generalized into three white races. The text describes them as follows.

p080.s8.b2: In southern France and Spain the New Stone Age went together with sun worship, and great stones were raised to the sun, as later at Stonehenge. In Brittany, after more than fifteen hundred years of Christianity, people still keep New Stone Age charms and thunderstones. It shows how stubbornly old beliefs survive.

p080.s8.b3.q: But it is a fallacy to presume to classify the white peoples as Nordic, Alpine, and Mediterranean.

p080.s8.b4: The text says that distinctions once fairly clear have become impossible to identify because of widespread blending; even in 3000 B.C. the social groups were no more of one race than the present inhabitants of North America. Here the text itself draws a boundary against treating racial types as fixed categories.
p080.s9.b0: Paper 80 shows that the roots of Western civilization lie in the meeting and mixing of many peoples, and in the accidents of climate and terrain. At the same time it records again and again that wherever civilization advanced, decline followed as spiritual standards faded. The paper quietly teaches that achievements in technique and art alone cannot preserve a civilization.

p081.lead: From farming and tools to cities, commerce, and fifteen conditions for keeping it alive: the civilization humanity has built since Adam, and how it can be preserved.

p081.foot.text: Sponsored by an Archangel of Nebadon

p081.s0.h: Introduction — Evolution That Cannot Be Stopped
p081.s0.b0: Paper 81 brings the long series of papers on the history of Urantia to a close at the threshold of modern civilization. It was sponsored by an Archangel of Nebadon. The missions of Caligastia and Adam did not turn out as planned, yet the basic organic evolution of the human species kept carrying the races forward. The violet race was smaller in number than intended, but its influence produced an advance in civilization since Adam’s day that far exceeded mankind’s progress during the almost one million years before.

p081.s0.b1.q: Evolution can be delayed but it cannot be stopped.

p081.s0.b2: The first sections describe in turn agriculture and tools, cities and commerce, the mixed races, and cultural society; the final section sets out fifteen conditions on which the maintenance of civilization depends. It is a paper in which historical narrative turns into reflection on the society we live in today.
p081.s1.h: I. The Cradle of Civilization — What Climate Accomplished
p081.s1.b0: For some thirty-five thousand years after Adam, the cradle of civilization was southwestern Asia, stretching from the Nile valley through Mesopotamia to Turkestan, and the decisive factor was climate. When the land elevations and climatic changes ended around 15,000 B.C., civilization came to a world-wide standstill. Then climatic evolution accomplished what all other efforts had failed to do: it compelled the hunter to become a herder and a farmer.
p081.s1.b1: The farmer was looked down on for a long time. Because the early agriculturists so generally used slaves, tilling the soil was thought menial, and even in the days of Cain and Abel the sacrifices of the pastoral life were held in greater esteem than the offerings of agriculture. The paper corrects this prejudice.

p081.s1.b2.q: the idea that soil toil is a curse, whereas it is the greatest of all blessings

p081.s1.b3: In regions with a large infusion of violet blood, whole tribes sometimes passed directly from hunting to agriculture. In the highlands of northern Mesopotamia the improved wheat and barley of the Garden were cultivated, and a diet that combined wheat and rice, vegetables and meat, greatly increased the health and vigor of the ancient peoples.
p081.s2.h: II. The Tools of Civilization — From Toil to Leisure for Thought
p081.s2.b0: The growth of culture is predicated on the development of the tools of civilization, and tools are effective only as they release human energy for higher tasks. The paper reminds today’s reader that our early ancestors had almost none of the leisure we now enjoy.

head: The first four great advances

p081.s2.b2: Just as the simple story of how fire began gave way to the legend of Prometheus, people have long attached supernatural explanations to whatever they could not understand. But the frank and fearless search for true causes gave birth to modern science.

p081.s2.b3.q: It turned astrology into astronomy, alchemy into chemistry, and magic into medicine.

p081.s2.b4: Shelter advanced from caves to huts of wood and stone, and then to the making of bricks. The mud-plastered hut suggested basketry and pottery, and when such a hut accidentally burned, the art of baking was discovered. The paper adds that although machines may create temporary problems, their ultimate benefits are beyond reckoning.
p081.s3.b0: As the grasslands of Turkestan began to dry out from about 12,000 B.C., the higher types of Andites turned to trade and manufacture. The era of independent cities opened about twelve thousand years ago, but the paper warns us not to picture these early cities as refined places. Refuse piled up so that the ground level rose a foot or two every twenty-five years.
p081.s3.b1: A bronze culture older than 9000 B.C. has been found in Turkestan, and the mixing of copper and tin was discovered by an Adamsonite. The stone, bronze, and iron ages were not sharply divided; they existed side by side in different regions. By 5000 B.C. horses and wheeled vehicles were widely used in commerce and in war.

p081.s3.b2.q: The traveling trader and the roving explorer did more to advance historic civilization than all other influences combined.

p081.s3.b3: Military conquest, colonization, and missionary enterprise also spread culture, but they were secondary to trade. Trade brought different peoples into contact and speeded the cross-fertilization of cultures. The insight that meeting and exchange make civilizations grow is as true now as it was then.
p081.s4.h: IV. The Mixed Races — From Five to Three
p081.s4.b0: By the dawn of historic times, Eurasia, northern Africa, and the islands of the Pacific were covered by composite races formed by the repeated blending of the five basic stocks. The paper notes that the entire skeletal structure shows racial origin better than the skull alone, and explains that the five original types can be observed today in roughly three classes.

p081.s4.b2: This is a rough classification for the study of skeletons. The paper itself adds that these types appear mixed in northern China, the Levant, India, and South America, and that the Adamites and Nodites are now so blended that they can be identified only as a generalized group. The passage can be read as a picture of humanity as one intertwined family.
p081.s5.h: V. Cultural Society — A Guild of Earth Workers
p081.s5.b0: Biologic evolution and cultural civilization do not always go together, yet over the long course of history they are linked as cause and effect. Adam brought no strange arts to Urantia, but his inheritance raised the inherent abilities of the races and hastened progress. And the paper defines society this way: it is not a great club of inherited privilege into which everyone is born with free membership.

p081.s5.b1.q: an exalted and ever-advancing guild of earth workers

p081.s5.b2: Social association is a kind of survival insurance. People pay the premiums of self-sacrifice and restriction of personal liberty, and in return they receive the protection of the group. Rights carry duties, and group privileges call for group service.

p081.s5.b4.q: Liberty subject to group regulation is the legitimate goal of social evolution.

p081.s6.h: VI. The Maintenance of Civilization — Fifteen Conditions
p081.s6.b0: The descendants of the pure Adamic stock have all been dispersed, and there are no more Andites to stimulate civilization anew and no new sources of culture. Present civilization must therefore be maintained and cultivated. The paper names fifteen factors on which it rests.

p081.s6.b2: Several of these items speak directly to the social problems of our own day. The paper says that knowledge can be had by education, but wisdom, which is indispensable to true culture, can be secured only through experience. It advises that citizens learn one or more ordinary trades they can use in times of temporary unemployment before being trained in a specialty, and it warns that no civilization can long survive the maintenance of large classes of unemployed. The machine age becomes a calamity only for nations that fail to adjust wisely to the difficulties of transition.
p081.s6.b3: The greatest weight in this list falls on factors that cannot be seen. The paper observes that the twentieth century brought great advances in travel and communication, but that education and ethical appreciation have not kept pace. Just as no stream rises higher than its source, no civilization rises higher than the ideals its society holds.

p081.s6.b4.q: modern civilization is at a standstill in spiritual development and the safeguarding of the home institution.

p081.s6.b5.q: Intelligence may control the mechanism of civilization, wisdom may direct it, but spiritual idealism is the energy which really uplifts and advances human culture from one level of attainment to another.

p081.s6.b6: The paper foresees that humanity’s struggle will move from survival to a standard of living, and then to the quality of thinking. It also reminds us that society is not a divine institution but a phenomenon of evolution, so we should neither despise something because it is old nor embrace it uncritically because it is new. Great changes should not be attempted suddenly, yet moral and spiritual adjustments can be made at once, and this applies just as fully to the individual life.

p081.s6.b7.q: At first life was a struggle for existence; now, for a standard of living; next it will be for quality of thinking, the coming earthly goal of human existence.

p081.s6.b8: The remarks on leadership also deserve attention. Wisdom, insight, and foresight are indispensable to the survival of nations, and civilization is never really imperiled until able leadership vanishes. Yet such wise leadership has never exceeded one per cent of the population. That is why it matters so much that each of us become a wise and co-operative citizen in our own place.
p081.s7.b0: Paper 81 sums up the long struggle since Adam and tells us that modern culture is the fruit of that hard-won evolution. Since the invention of printing, humanity has raced ahead, quickly taking up the achievements of earlier generations. But what the paper finally stresses is people over devices and ideals over institutions.

p081.s7.b1.q: High civilizations are born of the sagacious correlation of material wealth, intellectual greatness, moral worth, social cleverness, and cosmic insight.

p082.lead: From the mating instinct through taboos and mores to the home: the long evolution of marriage, read as the history of sex control.

p082.foot.text: Presented by the Chief of Seraphim stationed on Urantia

p082.s0.h: Introduction — The Home, Chief Civilizing Agency
p082.s0.b0: Following the earlier papers on primitive institutions, Paper 82 looks at how the institution of marriage arose and was refined. The author, the Chief of Seraphim stationed on Urantia, defines marriage as man’s reactional adjustment to bisexuality, and family life as the sum total of all such adjustments. Marriage is not inherent in biologic evolution, but it is the basis of all social evolution and is therefore certain to endure in some form.

p082.s0.b1.q: Marriage has given mankind the home, and the home is the crowning glory of the whole long and arduous evolutionary struggle.

p082.s0.b2: Religious, social, and educational institutions are also needed for the survival of civilization, but it is in the home and the neighborhood that a child learns most of the essentials of living. The civilizations of the past kept evolving with a bare minimum of other institutions because the home was functioning well. The starting point of this paper is that the rich heritage humanity now possesses must likewise pass to the next generation through the home.

p082.s0.b3.q: The family as an educational institution must be maintained.

p082.s1.h: I. The Mating Instinct — A Test of Civilization
p082.s1.b0: The personality differences between men and women are great, yet the sex urge is enough to bring them together for the reproduction of the species. This instinct operated long before human beings knew love, devotion, or marital loyalty. The author distinguishes mating, an inherent tendency, from marriage, the evolutionary social repercussion of that tendency.
p082.s1.b1: The mating instinct, the paper says, is the one emotion that leads selfish people, under the guise of personal gratification, to place the welfare and perpetuation of the race above their own ease. In animals, instinctive periodicity restrains mating, but in man it does not, so society must impose self-control on the individual. The paper also observes that as food becomes more plentiful, the sex urge tends to become dominant.
p082.s1.b2: The author says that the sex regulations connected with marriage reveal two things. One is the relative progress of a civilization, which has increasingly demanded that the sex urge be gratified in useful channels and according to the mores. The other is the amount of Andite stock in a people; this inheritance added imagination and aesthetic sense, and so allowed sex to be expressed in both the highest and the lowest ways. Greater sensitivity brings with it a greater task of self-control.

p082.s1.b3.q: Self-control, more and more self-control, is the ever-increasing demand of advancing mankind.

p082.s1.b4: The statement that the intelligent submission of this impulse to the regulations of society is the supreme test of the actuality of any civilization carries real weight. Secrecy, insincerity, and hypocrisy may hide the problem, but they do not solve it, nor do they bring ethical progress. An honest approach to sex is itself a measure of a civilization’s maturity.
p082.s2.h: II. The Restrictive Taboos — Between Instinct and Ethics
p082.s2.b0: The author sums up the evolution of marriage as the history of sex control through social, religious, and civil restrictions. Nature takes no interest in individuals or in morals; it insists only on reproduction and leaves the resulting problems to society.

p082.s2.b1.q: This social conflict consists in the unending war between basic instincts and evolving ethics.

p082.s2.b2: The early races had little regulation, but as soon as social groups formed, marriage rules and restrictions grew up. Even crude taboos, by separating the sexes, fostered peace, order, and industry, and from them came the customs of dress, ornament, and religious practice, and even the ideas of vice, crime, and sin. Women were always bound by more taboos than men, and married women were marked off by such signs as hair arrangement, the veil, or a ring.

p082.s2.b3.q: But all ancient peoples should always be studied and judged in the light of the moral standards of the mores of their own times.

p082.s2.b4: This principle is the key to reading the whole paper. The strange and sometimes harsh customs that follow are not there to be mocked or condemned by today’s standards; they should be read as traces of the path human beings have found between instinct and ethics.
p082.s3.h: III. Early Marriage Mores — Marriage as Status, Duty, and Test
p082.s3.b0: Marriage has always had two realms: the mores and laws that regulate the outward side of mating, and the secret, personal relations of man and woman. Individuals have always rebelled against the regulations society imposes, and this is the root of the age-old sex problem. Even so, the races that exalted and practiced marriage evolved to higher levels and survived in greater numbers.

p082.s3.b1.q: Marriage standards have always been a true indicator of the current power of the mores and the functional integrity of the civil government.

p082.s3.b3: The ways of qualifying for marriage changed as well. Tribes that had demanded feats of thievery introduced athletic contests in place of raids, and as wife purchase declined, riddle contests appeared. Later still, the woman’s side tested a man’s ability to hunt, fight, and provide for a family, or the groom proved his worth by working at least a year in the bride’s home. The belief that the unmarried could not enter the spirit world even led to child marriages and marriages for the dead.

p082.s3.b5: The paper also describes the custom of widows dying on their husbands’ graves, and trial marriages in which the couple married only after pregnancy was confirmed. The author says these trial marriages were free from every semblance of license and were sincere tests of fertility, and then draws a pointed comparison for modern readers: those who marry with the thought of convenient divorce in the back of their minds are entering a form of trial marriage far beneath the honest adventures of their ancestors.
p082.s4.h: IV. Marriage under the Property Mores — Stability and Its Shadow

p082.s4.b0.q: Property has been the stabilizer of marriage; religion, the moralizer.

p082.s4.b1: In primitive society marriage was more a business investment than a romance, arranged by parents and elders for the good of the group. As a result, the marriages of early tribes lasted longer than those of many modern peoples. But the same property idea treated a woman as a possession handed from father to husband, and regarded adultery as theft, a violation of the husband’s property rights.

p082.s4.b2.q: Modern sex jealousy is not innate; it is a product of the evolving mores.

p082.s4.b3: The observation that primitive man was not jealous but simply guarding his property reminds us that even feelings we take to be natural were shaped by history. The chastity taboo also began as a phase of the property mores and gave rise to the custom of the bride price; when it hardened too far, it produced the practice of confining girls and the tragedy of rejected brides. A device for stability could at the same time become a device for oppression.
p082.s5.h: V. Endogamy and Exogamy — Marriage Widens the Peace
p082.s5.b0: Primitive man early observed that outbreeding improved the quality of offspring. Inbreeding was not always bad, but the results of inbreeding among defective stocks made a strong impression, and the taboo against close marriage became fixed. The author is clear that there is no biologic instinct against in-marriage; such restrictions are wholly a matter of taboo.

p082.s5.b2: Superior groups, when isolated, always returned to consanguineous mating. The Nodites were one of the great in-marriage groups for over one hundred and fifty thousand years, and brother and sister marriages were common in early Egypt, Mesopotamia, and the lands once occupied by the Andites. Abraham himself married his half sister, but the later mores of the Jews did not allow such unions. That the same custom could be permitted in one age and forbidden in another shows clearly the evolutionary character of the mores.

p082.s5.b3.q: Outmarriage itself was a peace promoter

p082.s5.b4: Marriage between tribes lessened hostility and produced alliances, and together with adventure and exploration it furthered the cross-fertilization of racial cultures. The fact that the taboos extended even to in-laws with no blood relation shows that these rules came from sociology, not biology. Learning to become family with strangers was the very process by which the circle of peace was widened.
p082.s6.h: VI. Racial Mixtures — Telling Prejudice from Biology

p082.s6.b0.q: There are no pure races in the world today.

p082.s6.b1: The last section treats a sensitive subject from a biological point of view. According to the author, all existing races are already much mixed. The paper divides the Sangik races into primary and secondary, but adds that the secondary races also had many desirable traits and were in some respects superior to the primary races. It reads less as a simple ranking than as a statement that each stock has its own contribution to make.
p082.s6.b2: The standard the paper uses is not color but the quality of the stocks. The union of superior stocks increases vigor and creativity, while the union of degenerate stocks yields unsatisfactory results even within one race. Most objections to race mixture, in the paper’s judgment, arise from social and cultural prejudice rather than biology, and the danger of disharmony has been greatly exaggerated.

p082.s6.b3.q: The chief troubles of "half-breeds" are due to social prejudices.

p082.s6.b5: The conclusion of this section turns our attention away from the boundaries between races and toward caring for the biological quality of humanity within every people. A present-day reader will be closer to the paper’s intent by taking this passage not as grounds for looking down on any group, but as a warning that prejudice makes problems larger than they really are.
p082.s7.b0: Paper 82 shows that marriage did not descend from heaven as a finished institution. It was shaped little by little, through taboo, property, and religion, amid the unending clash of instinct and ethics. The way was clumsy and at times cruel, yet at its end humanity gained the home, its crowning glory. We who come after are responsible for guarding that inheritance with self-control and honesty.
